locator.quote: Kolatt et al. (1995) locate the approximate centre of the extended GA overdensity at (ℓ, b, v) ∼ (320°, 0°, 4000 km s-1) based on their smoothed reconstructed mass-density field. The uncertainty in this position is ∼17° as a result of the applied smoothing of 1200 km s-1; this smoothing is necessary given the sparsely sampled data (Kolatt et al. 1995).

disputes.claim: A smoothed reconstruction of the mass-density field by Kolatt et al. (1995), as Woudt et al. report it, puts the approximate centre of the extended overdensity at (ℓ, b, v) ∼ (320°, 0°, 4000 km/s), uncertain by about 17°, away from the direction the flow model imposes.

record.name: Great Attractor
record.notes: The position is the standard mass-concentration model of Lynden-Bell et al.: the concentration is placed in the direction of the elliptical galaxies' bulk flow relative to the CMB, and only its distance and the infall it induces at the Local Group are fitted. The direction is therefore the bulk flow's, kept with its own errors among the values, and Table 2 prints none for it in the standard MC solution. The distance is in km/s of the Hubble flow in the CMB frame, so it needs no Hubble constant. The paper's Galactic l and b, printed in whole degrees, predate the Hipparcos definition and are taken in it. The paper models a point concentration and gives no extent, so the structure is a point. Left out: the excess mass, in solar masses, which univ-model has no unit for; the Table 2 solution that fits a bulk flow beside the mass concentration; and the redshift peak of da Costa et al. that the abstract quotes, another paper's measurement. The paper calls the concentration in Centaurus the new supergalactic center. Woudt et al. find the Norma cluster close to the predicted centre and at the bottom of its potential well, and note that the attractor lies largely behind the Milky Way, which hid the galaxies that early estimates of its mass could not find; the cluster's position and heliocentric mean velocity are kept as published. Tully et al. find the Laniakea flows converging toward the Norma and Centaurus clusters near the Great Attractor; their attractor centroid is the Laniakea file's position, kept here as values. Not read: the Nature paper of Kraan-Korteweg et al. that identified the Norma cluster in the attractor region, Kolatt et al. (read only as Woudt et al. report them), and the earlier letter of Dressler et al.
